divePrompts.text: Something that shows a copy or a retelling can change what a thing means.
A method that cannot answer every question.
Someone whose part in a discovery is easy to overlook.
Something whose date or age is not certain.
A case where a name or a label shapes what people believe.
A 'first' that depends on what you count.
A time when the senses needed a check.
A measurement or forecast that carries uncertainty.
A result shaped by who or what was chosen to look at.
A map, model or picture that leaves something out on purpose.
A case where a pattern was not enough, and a proof or a test was needed.
A source made for a purpose that shapes what it says.
An honest report that was still mistaken.
Knowledge made by many people, not by one.
Something that changes when it moves between languages or words.
A record that tells you one thing, but not another.

facets.text: Loud's 1888 patent came decades before the Biro pen, so who 'invented the ballpoint' depends on what you count.
A patent records a design and a claim. It does not show whether the pen worked or sold.
A patent is written to claim a design, so it says what the inventor wanted to protect.
Bíró's practical pen was made with his chemist brother György and others.
It separates Loud's patent from Bíró's later practical pen and ink.
The museum dates the pen 1945–1948: a range, not one year.
Its record names László Bíró and his brother, not one inventor alone.
One surviving pen does not show how many were made or how well they sold.
A modern model built from the drawing shows one way it could work. It is not Loud's pen.
Its materials are modern, so it leaves out what an 1888 pen was made of.
A controlled test of modern models cannot tell us how the historical pens behaved.
The 'best' pen depended on which surfaces were tested.
'True wootz of ancient Damascus' sold the blade before anyone checked it.
A seller's sign is written to sell.
One test billet is one case, not a rule.
Hesper's forge in the game is a simple model, not a working recipe.
It did not match the blade, but one billet cannot show every crucible steel.
A simple forge model cannot show the skill real crucible steel needs.
It records a sale, but says nothing about the steel.
A ledger is kept to track money and goods, so that is what it records.
The pattern looked like wootz to the eye. The etched section showed welded layers.
A schematic section still needs a trained assayer to confirm it.
'Probably eighteenth century': the museum says how sure it is.
These are ingots, the raw material, not finished blades.
'Damascus' alone does not name one recipe.
One word covers two different ways of making steel.
Pattern welding and crucible ('watered') steel are different crafts, even when people use one name.
An essay about techniques cannot identify any particular blade.
Nobody knows the exact length of the stadion he used, so his accuracy is uncertain.
His method reached us only through later writers.
'About 240 BCE': even the date of his measurement is an estimate.
'The first scientist' is a modern title. People in many places tested ideas before him.
He used experiments to test claims about light and seeing.
He did not trust what seemed obvious about seeing. He tested claims with experiments.
One written description survives. None of his clay type does.
Clay type in China, metal type in Korea, Gutenberg later: 'first' depends on what you count.
Printing from carved blocks was already in use. His work built on others'.
We know only that he was active in the 1040s, from one later book.
Accounts credit his calculations, but exactly who did which part is debated.
The Great Trigonometrical Survey was team work.
People who lived near the mountain already had names for it.
Many people in Brazil call him the inventor of the airplane. Others name the Wright brothers.
His 1906 flight had a crowd and officials. The Wrights' 1903 flights had few witnesses.
Some places let some women vote earlier, in local or limited elections.
Large petitions: many people made the change.
Māori women also voted in 1893. A story about one leader can hide many others.
Earlier writers also defended women, for example Christine de Pizan in 1405.
Christine de Pizan wrote in 1405 and is named less often.
Every restoration kept some layers and lost others.
The gate label had to say honestly what was kept and lost.
Witnesses honestly reported things they had only heard.
Where each witness stood decided what they could see.
1, 2, 4, 8, 16 panes, and then 31.
Every map left out some layers.
Each map was made for one person's need.
The sorter learned only from the examples it was given.
A machine that copies examples cannot sort a fruit it has never seen.
My reaction time pushed every echo time the same way.
My ears and hands were part of the measuring instrument.
The guild meeting and the market gave very different answers.
A leading question changed the answer.
Tavi, loma, kethe, belun: words English needs a phrase for.
The back-translation came back changed.
Each poster was framed for someone's purpose.
Each poster left out most of the painting.
The same true scene told three stories.
My ears heard a climb that never ends. The tuning glass showed a loop.
Maren honestly believed her bells climb forever.
A 70% forecast that stays dry is not wrong.
Twelve days are too few to judge a forecaster.
Each retelling of the rumour filled a gap with a guess.
The tea seller passed it on in good faith.
